strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing the gap between task-specific CAD models and the industrial standard B-rep format; unified framework is conceptually appealing and practical

Strong empirical results across all tasks: 48.7% CD improvement in reverse engineering, 25% accuracy improvement in completion, 99% ACC_cmd in error correction, and competitive CAD-QA performance on a smaller model

Thoughtful treatment of modeling ambiguity (Figure 5) with statistical analysis showing domain understanding; acknowledges fundamental evaluation challenge that multiple CAD sequences produce identical geometry

Comprehensive multi-task evaluation with task-appropriate baselines and metrics; solid ablation studies (Table 3) validating design choices (CoCa over CLIP, frozen encoder, model scale, Stage 1 importance)

Sound design decisions with clear justification: CoCa framework choice for fine-grained+global feature extraction, Python-like code leveraging LLM programming knowledge, strategic freezing of B-rep encoder
Clear presentation with effective figures and well-structured methodology; reproducibility aided by public DeepCAD dataset and detailed architectural descriptions
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing components (CAD-Llama code format, UV-Net encoder, CoCa framework, standard two-stage training) without introducing new methods, algorithms, or theoretical insights

Narrow evaluation scope: single dataset (DeepCAD 170K) for primary evaluation; no cross-dataset testing or evaluation on real-world industrial CAD models from other software (Fusion 360, Solidworks); unclear generalization beyond DeepCAD format

Unfair baseline comparisons limit credibility: (1) Error correction compares B-rep vs. rendered 2D images for GPT/Gemini, (2) ReCAD uses different OpenSCAD dataset format, (3) CAD-Llama uses textual annotations vs. B-rep—different modalities not purely model comparisons; paper acknowledges but doesn't provide controlled experiments

Fundamental evaluation metric limitations unresolved: ACC_cmd still penalizes geometrically equivalent CAD sequences despite Figure 5 analysis; Invalid Ratio (IR) not precisely defined; parameter tolerance δ for ACC_param unclear; no proposed solution to modeling ambiguity problem

Missing critical analysis: no failure case analysis or error types studied; no discussion of model performance on different CAD complexity levels; no prompt sensitivity analysis for Stage 2; no computational cost comparison (training time, inference speed, memory); efficiency vs. baselines unclear given size differences (1.5B vs. 7B)

B-rep dependency limits practical applicability: requires B-rep input (not always available); paper doesn't address how to obtain B-rep from point clouds or images; real-world applicability constrained by availability of B-rep exports from diverse CAD software

Stage 1 pre-training necessity shown empirically (~8% improvement) but not theoretically justified; no exploration of alternative pre-training objectives or analysis of why reverse engineering specifically benefits downstream tasks
Reproducibility gaps: no mention of code/model release promised; missing implementation details (δ value for ACC_param, learning rate schedules, optimization specifics, training convergence criteria)

Limited architectural novelty: projector is only 3 linear layers + GELU; standard frozen-encoder + LLM concatenation approach; loss function weights (λ_con=1, λ_cap=2) borrowed from CoCa without CAD domain validation

Generalization claims not empirically validated: 'superior generalization across diverse tasks' only shown within DeepCAD; no cross-dataset evaluation; no comparison with end-to-end trained models; missing experiments on model complexity scaling

strengths: Addresses practical industrial problem: focuses on B-rep format used by real CAD systems, unlike existing work emphasizing point clouds/images
Unified multi-task framework: single architecture handles reverse engineering, completion, error correction, and CAD-QA without task-specific modifications
Clever representation design: conversion to Python-like CAD code leverages LLM programming reasoning; explicit object-oriented structure well-justified
Principled multimodal alignment: CoCa framework combining contrastive and captioning losses outperforms CLIP-based alternatives
Comprehensive evaluation: four diverse tasks, multiple baselines per task, rich metrics (ACC_cmd, ACC_param, Chamfer distance, invalid ratio, VLM scores), thorough ablations
Honest treatment of limitations: acknowledges modeling ambiguity (Figure 5) with statistical evidence, showing 14.14% of low-CD results have low ACC_cmd
Excellent geometric quality: achieves 0.464×10⁻³ Chamfer distance (52% improvement over CADCL) with very low invalid ratio (0.86%)
Strong implementation details: Appendix provides concrete hyperparameters, layer specifications, and training configurations supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: UV-Net, CoCa, and Qwen are existing components; contribution is primarily orchestration rather than methodological innovation
Modest performance gains: ACC_cmd actually 89.34% vs CADCL's 90.31% (regression); CAD-QA 79% vs PointLLM's 81% with model size difference unaccounted for
Single-dataset evaluation: only DeepCAD (170K) tested; no cross-dataset validation or evaluation on other CAD systems (Fusion 360, SolidWorks, FreeCAD)
Unclear generalization: Python-like code format is dataset-specific; no analysis of adaptation to different CAD representations or real-world CAD diversity
Baseline comparison fairness: error correction compares 3D B-rep (BrepCoder) to 2D images (GPT/Gemini); ReCAD comparison uses different dataset; CAD-QA training protocol under-specified
Insufficient failure analysis: no systematic error categorization, investigation of performance degradation with model complexity, or analysis of real-world vs. artificial error patterns

Modeling ambiguity unresolved: while acknowledged, remains unclear if this reflects fundamental CAD properties or indicates model doesn't learn true design logic; 11.97% of results show geometry failures
Missing computational analysis: no inference time, memory requirements, or scalability analysis compared to baselines—critical for practical deployment

Hyperparameter choices lack justification: no sensitivity analysis for τ=0.7, λ weights, or projector architecture; frozen encoder ablation shows worse unfrozen performance but explanation speculative

Limited downstream task scope: completion retention ratio (30-50%) arbitrary without ablation; error types (permutation, noise) artificial; CAD-QA restricted to multiple-choice on small SGP-Bench (1K models)
Generalization concerns: no real industrial CAD evaluation, user studies on design intent alignment, or analysis of boundary conditions and failure modes
Reproducibility gaps: DeepCAD release status unclear, B-rep preprocessing details sparse, checkpoint selection criteria not discussed
